facts.statement: Teratophoneus is a genus of tyrannosaurine theropod dinosaur named for its meaning of "monstrous murderer" in Greek.
facts.quote: Teratophoneus ("monstrous murderer"; Greek: teras, "monster" and phoneus, "murderer") is a genus of tyrannosaurine theropod dinosaur

facts.statement: The only known species of Teratophoneus is T. curriei, which honors paleontologist Philip J. Currie.
facts.quote: It contains a single known species, T. curriei, named in honor of paleontologist Philip J. Currie.

facts.statement: Teratophoneus was named by Thomas D. Carr and colleagues in 2011.
facts.quote: Teratophoneus was named by Thomas D. Carr, Thomas E. Williamson, Brooks B. Britt, and Ken Stadtman in 2011.

facts.statement: A new Teratophoneus specimen was discovered in the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in 2017.
facts.quote: In 2017, a new specimen of Teratophoneus was discovered in the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument and airlifted to the Natural History Museum of Utah in Salt Lake City.

facts.statement: In 2021, fossils belonging to four or five individuals of Teratophoneus were described.
facts.quote: Later, in 2021, fossils belonging to 4 or 5 individuals were described in the same study.

facts.statement: Carr et al. estimated the subadult holotype of Teratophoneus to be about 6 meters long and 667 kg.
facts.quote: According to an estimate by Carr et al., it was about 6 m long and 667 kg.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum adult size of Teratophoneus to be 8 meters long and 2.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul gave an estimation of 8 m long and 2.5 MT for the maximum adult size.

facts.statement: In 2021, Yun estimated the subadult Teratophoneus to be approximately 6.1 meters long and 1 metric ton based on frontal bone size.
facts.quote: In 2021, based on the size of the frontal bone (similar to that of Lythronax), Yun moderated the size of the subadult at approximately 6.1 m long and 1 MT.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the deeper skull of Teratophoneus may have allowed for stronger jaw muscles and increased bite force.
facts.quote: The skull of Teratophoneus is also comparably deeper. It is unclear if there was a specific reason for these differences, but the extra depth may have allowed for stronger jaw muscles, thus increasing the bite force of Teratophoneus.

facts.statement: Loewen et al. (2013) confirmed that Teratophoneus belongs to the tyrannosaurid subfamily Tyrannosaurinae.
facts.quote: Loewen et al. (2013) conducted a phylogenetic analysis of the family Tyrannosauridae and confirmed the assignment of Teratophoneus to the tyrannosaurid subfamily Tyrannosaurinae.

facts.statement: Voris et al. (2020) placed Teratophoneus in a subclade with Dynamoterror and Lythronax, later named Teratophoneini in 2024.
facts.quote: In 2020, when describing the genus Thanatotheristes, Voris et al., 2020 found Teratophoneus to be in a subclade alongside Dynamoterror and Lythronax. This clade was named the Teratophoneini in 2024.

facts.statement: A 2021 study of a bone bed suggests Teratophoneus may have been a social pack-hunter.
facts.quote: A bone bed of fossils from the Rainbows and Unicorns Quarry in Southern Utah's Kaiparowits Formation described in 2021 attributed to Teratophoneus suggests that the genus may have been a social pack-hunter.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, Teratophoneus lived on Laramidia near the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: During the Late Cretaceous, the site within the Kaiparowits Formation was located on Laramidia near its eastern shore on the Western Interior Seaway, a large inland sea that split North America into two island landmasses, the other one being Appalachia in the east.

facts.statement: Teratophoneus lived on an ancient floodplain with wetland peat swamps, ponds, and lakes bordered by highlands.
facts.quote: The plateau where dinosaurs lived was an ancient floodplain dominated by large channels and an abundance of wetland peat swamps, ponds, and lakes and was bordered by highlands.

facts.statement: The climate where Teratophoneus lived was wet and humid.
facts.quote: The climate was wet and humid, supporting an array of different and diverse groups of organisms.

facts.statement: Deinosuchus was the apex predator in the same environment as Teratophoneus.
facts.quote: Other paleofauna present in the Kaiparowits Formation included chondrichthyans (sharks and rays), frogs, salamanders, turtles, lizards, and crocodilians, with Deinosuchus being the apex predator.

facts.statement: The genus Teratophoneus was established by Carr et al. in 2011.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Carr et al., 2011

facts.statement: Teratophoneus curriei lived approximately 77 to 76 million years ago in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Teratophoneus curriei es la única especie conocida del género extinto Teratophoneus (gr. "monstruo asesino") de dinosaurio terópodo tiranosáurido de finales del período Cretácico durante el Campaniense, hace aproximadamente 77 a 76 millones de años, en lo que ahora es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The Teratophoneus specimen was not fully developed and was estimated by Carr et al. to be about 6 meters long and 667 kg.
facts.quote: El espécimen de Teratophoneus no estaba completamente desarrollado,y de acuerdo con la estimación de Carr et al. medía cerca de 6 metros de largo y 667 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: In 2021, Yun estimated the subadult Teratophoneus to be about 6.1 meters long and 1 metric ton based on frontal bone size.
facts.quote: En 2021, según el tamaño del hueso frontal, similar al de Lythronax, Yun moderó el tamaño del subadulto a aproximadamente 6,1 metros de largo y 1 tonelada de masa corporal.

facts.statement: It is unclear why the skull is deeper, but it may have allowed for stronger jaw muscles and increased bite force.
facts.quote: No es claro sí había una razón específica para esta diferencias, pero la mayor altura puede haberle permitido alojar músculos mandibulares más fuertes, incrementando la fuerza de mordida de Teratophoneus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Teratophoneus were found in Utah, USA.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en Utah, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The genus Teratophoneus was named in 2011 by Thomas D. Carr, Thomas E. Williamson, Brooks B. Britt, and Ken Stadtman.
facts.quote: Teratophoneus fue nombrado por Thomas D. Carr, Thomas E. Williamson, Brooks B. Britt y Ken Stadtman en el año de 2011

facts.statement: The species name curriei honors the Canadian paleontologist Philip J. Currie.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie homenajea al paleontólogo canadiense Philip J. Currie.

facts.statement: The genus name Teratophoneus is derived from the Greek words teras, meaning "monster", and phoneus, meaning "murderer".
facts.quote: El nombre científico del género se deriva de los términos griegos teras, "monstruo" y phoneus, "asesino".

facts.statement: A 2013 phylogenetic analysis confirmed that Teratophoneus belongs to the subfamily Tyrannosaurinae.
facts.quote: Loewen et al. (2013) realizaron un análisis filogenético y confirmaron la asignación de Teratophoneus a la subfamilia de terópodos Tyrannosaurinae.

facts.statement: Teratophoneus was closely related to the large tyrannosaurids Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus, being more primitive than them but more advanced than Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: Teratophoneus estaba cercanamente relacionado con los grandes tiranosáuridos Tarbosaurus y Tyrannosaurus si bien era más primitivo que estos, pero a su vez era más avanzado que Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2020, a study by Voris et al. placed Teratophoneus in an unnamed subclade with Dynamoterror and Lythronax.
facts.quote: En 2020, al describir el género Thanatotheristes, Voris et al. , 2020 encontró que Teratophoneus estaba en un subclade junto con Dynamoterror y Lythronax.

facts.statement: Radiometric dating indicates the Kaiparowits Formation was deposited between 76.1 and 74.0 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: La datación radiométrica de argón-argón indica que la Formación Kaiparowits se depositó hace entre 76,1 y 74,0 millones de años, durante la etapa Campaniense del período Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: Teratophoneus lived during the middle of the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Esta fecha significa que Teratophoneus vivió en la mitad de esta etapa del Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: During its time, the Kaiparowits site was located near the western coast of the Niobrara Sea, an inland sea that divided North America into Laramidia and Appalachia.
facts.quote: Durante este período, el sitio de Kaiparowits se localizaba cerca de la costa occidental del Mar de Niobrara, un gran mar interno que dividía a Norteamérica en dos masas terrestres, Laramidia al oeste y Appalachia al este.

facts.statement: The dinosaurs lived on a floodplain featuring peat swamps surrounded by highlands.
facts.quote: La planicie en la que los dinosaurios vivieron era una antigua planicie de inundación con pantanos de turba rodeados de tierras altas.

facts.statement: A 2021 description of a bonebed in the Kaiparowits Formation suggests that Teratophoneus was a social hunter.
facts.quote: Un lecho óseo de fósiles de la Cantera de Arcoíris y Unicornios en la Formación Kaiparowits del sur de Utah descrito en 2021 atribuido a Teratophoneus sugiere que el género era un cazador social.

facts.statement: Fossils consisting of four or possibly five individuals aged between 4 and 22 years suggest a mass mortality event, possibly caused by floods, cyanobacteria toxicity, fires, or droughts.
facts.quote: Los fósiles, que consisten en cuatro o posiblemente cinco animales de entre 4 y 22 años de edad, sugieren un evento de mortalidad masiva, posiblemente causado por inundaciones, o menos probablemente por toxicosis por cianobacterias, incendios o sequías.

facts.statement: The fact that all preserved animals died in a short period strengthens the argument for gregarious behavior in tyrannosaurids, as bonebeds of Teratophoneus, Albertosaurus, and Daspletosaurus suggest this behavior may have been widespread among tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: El hecho de que todos los animales preservados murieran en un corto período de tiempo fortalece aún más el argumento del comportamiento gregario en los tiranosáuridos, con lechos óseos de Teratophoneus, Albertosaurus y Daspletosaurus que muestran que el comportamiento potencial puede haber estado muy extendido entre los tiranosaurios en general.

facts.statement: Teratophoneus shared its environment with dromaeosaurids, the troodontid Talos sampsoni, ornithomimids like Ornithomimus velox, the tyrannosaurid Albertosaurus, ankylosaurids, hadrosaurids like Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus and Gryposaurus monumentensis, ceratopsians like Utahceratops gettyi, Nasutoceratops titusi, and Kosmoceratops richardsoni, and the oviraptorosaur Hagryphus giganteus.
facts.quote: Teratophoneus compartió su paleoambiente con otros terópodos como los dromeosáuridos, el trodóntido Talos sampsoni, ornitomímidos como Ornithomimus velox, el tiranosáurido Albertosaurus, anquilosáuridos, los hadrosáuridos Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus y Gryposaurus monumentensis, los ceratopsios Utahceratops gettyi, Nasutoceratops titusi y Kosmoceratops richardsoni y el ovirraptorosaurio Hagryphus giganteus.

facts.statement: The Kaiparowits Formation paleofauna included chondrichthyan fish (sharks and rays), frogs, salamanders, turtles, lizards, and crocodilians.
facts.quote: Entre la paleofauna presente en la Formación Kaiparowits se incluyen peces condrictios (tiburones y rayas), ranas, salamandras, tortugas, lagartos y crocodilianos.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Teratophoneus as Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
